regulations.name: IEC 60601-1-11:2015 + A1:2020 / EN 60601-1-11:2015 + A1:2021
regulations.description: Requirements for ME equipment used in home healthcare environment

tests.requirement: Instructions for use for ME equipment intended for use by a lay operator include easily understood diagrams, illustrations, or photographs of the fully assembled and ready-to-operate ME equipment including all controls, visual information signals, and indicators provided
tests.result_remark: Described in chapter 'SETUP AND OPERATING PROCEDURES' of operation guide

tests.requirement: Additional requirements for ME equipment start-up procedure

sub_items.requirement: Easily understood diagrams, illustrations, or photographs showing proper connection of the patient to the ME equipment, accessories and other equipment
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'SETUP AND OPERATING PROCEDURES' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: The time from switching 'on' until the ME equipment is ready for normal use, when it exceeds 15 s (see 15.4.4 of Part 1)
The time required for ME equipment to warm from the minimum storage temperature between uses until it is ready for intended use
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'MAINTENANCE' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: The time required for ME equipment to cool from the maximum storage temperature between uses until it is ready for intended use
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'MAINTENANCE' of operation guide

tests.requirement: Instructions for use for ME equipment intended for use by a lay operator include a description of generally known conditions in the home healthcare environment that can unacceptably affect the basic safety and essential performance of the ME equipment

sub_items.requirement: The steps that can be taken by the lay operator to identify and resolve the above conditions
At least the following issues are also included as applicable
The effects of lint, dust, light (including sunlight), etc.
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'MAINTENANCE' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: A list of known devices or other sources that can potentially cause interference problems
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'NOTICE' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: The effects of degraded sensors and electrodes, or loosened electrodes, that can degrade performance or cause other problems
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'MAINTENANCE' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: The effects caused by pets, pests or children
sub_items.result_remark: Described in chapter 'NOTICE' of operation guide

sub_items.requirement: The instructions for use explain the meaning of the IP classification marked on the ME equipment, and on any carrying case provided with the ME equipment as applicable

tests.requirement: Instructions for use include a troubleshooting guide for use when there are indications of a ME equipment malfunction during start-up or operation
tests.result_remark: Described in chapter 'TROUBLESHOOTING' of operation guide

tests.requirement: Troubleshooting guide discloses the necessary steps in the event of a technical alarm condition

semantic_fragments.content: IEC 60601-1-11 clauses 7.4.3 through 7.4.6 define requirements for instructions for use targeting lay operators in home healthcare environments. These include: (1) diagrams/illustrations of assembled ME equipment with controls and indicators; (2) start-up procedure documentation including patient connection diagrams, warm-up/cool-down times; (3) description of environmental conditions (lint, dust, light, interference sources, degraded sensors, pets/pests/children) that may affect safety and essential performance; (4) troubleshooting guides covering malfunction detection and technical alarm conditions. All applicable clauses were evaluated against the operation guide chapters 'SETUP AND OPERATING PROCEDURES', 'MAINTENANCE', 'NOTICE', and 'TROUBLESHOOTING'.
